1000265.etyen: Internationalism, based on Latin Plūtō (“Pluto, god of the underworld”), from Ancient Greek Πλούτων (Ploútōn, “Plouton, god of the underworld”), formed from πλοῦτος (ploûtos, “wealth, riches”) + -ων (-ōn, “possessive suffix”). The divine name therefore meant approximately “the rich one”, an epithet of the ruler of the underworld, associated not only with the dead but also with the riches and fertility contained within the earth. 1004873.etyen:
From Ghana (“Ghana (historical kingdom)”) + rike (“realm, kingdom, empire”), with the second element in the definite singular; literally “the Ghana realm”.
The historical name predates that of the modern state Ghana (“Ghana”). The medieval polity was called Wagadu by its rulers, while the name Ghana came from the ruler's title ghana, traditionally glossed as “war chief”. The further origin of the title is unknown.
Compare Danish Ghanariget and Swedish Ghanariket (“Ghana Empire”).

1005129.etyen:
